Electricity: ElectricalProgressive Mod
The mod adds electrical energy, electrical appliances, devices, weapons, and armor to the game. All this helps to ease (or not) survival in the game world, reduce the amount of routine, and diversify the gaming experience.

Basics
The law of conservation of energy states that energy does not appear from nowhere and does not disappear anywhere. Energy only transforms from one form to another or from one body to another. It's the same in the game.

The main source of mechanical energy is windmills. Using generators, you can convert mechanical energy into electrical energy. To do this, you need to transmit torque from the mill to the generator shaft using axles and/or gears. After that, the generator will start producing electricity.

Electrical energy can be transmitted via cables to consumers. Simply place cables on blocks in the desired direction. You can place up to 4 cables on each block face, directed in different directions. This allows you to route cables in any direction and branch the electrical circuit. The cable must be connected to the iron plate of the electrical appliance for it to start working. Electrical appliances, metal blocks, and feedthroughs can also conduct current.

Since the wind does not always blow at full strength, the energy generated by generators may not be enough to power all electrical appliances. To avoid this, you need to connect your electrical circuit to accumulator(s). They will constantly accumulate electrical energy and release it into the circuit to power devices at any moment, even when there is no wind.

To save energy, some appliances need to be disconnected from the circuit when not in use. A manual switch is used for this. Install it on the circuit section where you need to quickly cut off power.

For some devices that still require mechanical energy to operate, a motor will be needed. It converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. It needs to be connected via an axle to the device. When turned on, the motor will try to deliver maximum power to the shaft, so make sure the circuit has enough energy.

Electricity: Motors and Generators
Motors and generators in the mod allow converting electrical energy into mechanical energy and vice versa. To do this, you need to connect cables to them and connect via an axle.

Features of Game Mechanics
Motors and generators simulate the behavior of such real-life devices as closely as possible. DC machines were used as an example. Therefore, to better understand how to use them and in what situations, you need to understand the laws by which they operate.
All rotating mechanisms in the game, including axles and gears, have two basic parameters: torque and resistance. Torque characterizes the force with which the mechanism rotates the shaft, and resistance characterizes the friction forces and losses that may occur during their operation. The torque of axles and gears is zero. The game engine sums all torques and calculates the shaft speed and its acceleration/deceleration. If the torque is greater than the resistance, the shaft speed will increase. If vice versa, it will decrease. Moreover, both of these parameters change according to certain laws. Usually, resistance increases with speed.

Generators
In the mod, generators have the following additional parameters:
I_max – maximum energy output value;
speed_max – maximum rated rotation speed;
resistance_factor – multiplier for resistance;
resistance_load – constant component of resistance (achieved at I_max).

The generator's energy output depends only on the shaft speed and is calculated proportionally to the shaft speed. When exceeding speed_max, the output is power = I_max.
At the same time, the resistance first increases linearly, and when speed_max is exceeded, it increases quadratically. Also, the resistance is directly proportional to the load of the electrical circuit on this generator. Therefore, when there is no consumption, the generator will create minimal resistance.

Motors
In the mod, motors have the following additional parameters:
I_min – minimum energy value required for the motor to start operating;
I_max – maximum energy consumption value;
torque_max – maximum torque;
kpd_max – efficiency;
speed_max – maximum rated rotation speed;
resistance_factor – multiplier for resistance.

The motor produces torque directly proportional to the energy available to it. Additionally, the motor takes into account its own efficiency.

The motor's resistance is calculated similarly to the generator, except resistance_load is zero.

Electricity: Current Behavior, Voltage
Electric current now flows through conductors, obeying the laws of physics. Some may need to open their physics textbook again!

Features of the New Behavior
Electric current moves through conductors in the form of energy packets, except in instant mode. Energy packets move along the shortest path from current sources to consumers. Also, cables and devices now have their own electrical conductor parameters: resistivity (depends on material), cross-sectional area, maximum current (exceeding risks burning out), maximum voltage. The current value is calculated according to Ohm's law for a circuit section, for all energy packets passing at that moment through that face/block. The direction of energy movement is also taken into account: if energy moves in opposite directions, the corresponding currents are algebraically subtracted (a consequence of Kirchhoff's first law). To prevent cables from burning out, they can be thickened. To do this, take a cable of the same type as the one already placed and click on it while holding the Shift key. This way you can increase the current capacity in the circuit. However, note that losses in the conductor are calculated according to the Joule-Lenz law. An increase in the passing current greatly increases energy losses. To transmit energy over long distances, you can increase the voltage or use accumulators as buffer storage.

Voltages
Now, different devices require not only different amounts of energy but also different voltages. Exceeding the voltage for a device/cable risks it burning out. You can increase or decrease voltage using a transformer - it works bidirectionally. So be careful when connecting wires of different voltages! Higher voltage allows more energy to be transmitted through wires.

Interaction with the Environment
Now, uninsulated cables and metal blocks will deal damage to all entities upon contact. The higher the voltage in the circuit, the more damage they will receive. Burned devices and cables will also deal damage. Insulated cables and all operating devices are safe to touch.
All cables and devices have a moisture resistance parameter. If there is no moisture resistance, your device/cable risks burning out upon contact with rain, snow, hail, or spilled water nearby! Upon contact with lava, they burn out, break, and will most likely be destroyed. Be careful.

block-handbooktext-etermogenerator:
Converts thermal energy into electrical energy! Runs on anything that supports combustion. The higher the combustion temperature of the fuel, the higher the output power. The output power also slightly depends on the ambient temperature: the lower the ambient air temperature, the greater the energy output. It doesn't work by itself - it requires thermoelectric plates installed at the back.

Can be automatically loaded with fuel using hoppers.
block-handbooktext-termoplastini:
Thermoelectric plates are used in thermoelectric generators to convert thermal energy into electrical energy. The operating principle is based on the generation of thermoelectromotive force at the junction of two dissimilar metals. The temperature difference is created by the smoke from the burning fuel on one side and the ambient air on the other.

Placed behind the thermoelectric generator, up to 10 pieces. Can only be attached to the copper pad of the heat exchanger. Each subsequent section provides a smaller increase in power. A total of 10 thermoplates will give 100% power to the thermogenerator. Two generators can be used on the same set of thermoelectric plates.
block-handbooktext-esolargenerator: Converts light into electrical energy! The more sunlight hits the solar panel, the more energy it can produce. Blocks placed above the solar panel will reduce its efficiency. In late autumn and winter, sunlight decreases, leading to reduced efficiency.
